name: Sunday Harbour View Sukhumvit 50 Hotel
detail: The room is clean and tidy, with complete amenities. The bed is soft, and the pillows and bedding are clean and not old. The parking lot is spacious, the accommodation is quiet, and the staff is lovely with good service. I booked for under a thousand, overall it's very worth the price.

name: Solaria Nishitetsu Hotel Bangkok
detail: The staff's response is courteous and hospitable. The room is also clean. It's really convenient as it is directly connected to Asoke station. Although it faces the street, it is quiet, allowing for a good night's sleep. There is a coin laundry on the lobby floor. You pay 200 baht at the front desk to buy a token and detergent to use. There are only two machines, so it can get crowded depending on the time. I stayed in a twin room, but there was only one chair, and the table was small, making it difficult to find a place to put things. There is space in the room, so improvements would make it even more comfortable to stay. I feel very secure here, so I would like to stay again.

name: Palette Hi Hotel Bangkok
detail: Room with a good location Review of a room that is beautiful, clean, and offers great value. There are various types and sizes of rooms to choose from, ranging from standard rooms to executive suites, which are very spacious, perfect for relaxing whether you're here for work, a getaway with a partner, family, or hanging out with friends. It's very convenient for traveling, close to shopping malls, the sky train, fresh markets, and night markets. Importantly, the staff here are friendly, polite, and provide excellent service. Highly recommended! Hi Hotel Bangkok ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐🥰🥰

name: Boss Suites Nana
detail: The room was good. The shampoo and conditioner were not provided. The sauna was out of order, which was unfortunate. The breakfast buffet was very delicious. The staff was also kind. I would like to stay again.

name: Best Comfort Bangkok Hotel
detail: The price was very reasonable at around 6,000 yen per night, and the bed was spacious enough for two adults and two children aged 3 and 1 to sleep comfortably. Breakfast was for two adults but we were able to share with the children, which was a great help. The menu included sausage, chicken porridge, toast (with strawberry jam and butter), fried eggs, a small apple, orange juice, water, coffee, and tea, which was more than enough, especially the chicken porridge which was very delicious. The room had a bathtub, a sofa, and a larger refrigerator, allowing for a comfortable stay. Hairdryers are available for rent at the front desk, and shampoo and body soap, as well as soap, and two bottled waters are provided daily. Each guest also had one large towel. There is a pool and a gym on the rooftop, both well-maintained and pleasant to use. It is a bit of a hassle to have to leave the key at the front desk when going out, but the presence of staff all the time brings a sense of security. There are also a laundry service and a massage shop across from the hotel that charges 300 B for 60 minutes, which is convenient. Additionally, when staying at Ampar, it was very helpful that they allowed us to store our stroller and suitcase for free. The staff was impressive with their kindness and did not show any displeasure at all. It takes about 7-8 minutes to walk to Nana Station, but there is also a convenience store nearby, making the location quite good. Overall, it was a hotel that was very satisfactory.

name: Mode Sathorn Hotel
detail: The location is very good, next to Surasak BTS station. The room and bathroom are spacious and decorated modernly. I like the large glass windows in the bedroom and bathroom, offering a great view of the city from the 24th floor. The room is clean, and the staff provides good service. We went up for dinner at Rooftop Bar 37; the atmosphere is nice, and the food is delicious. The staff is very attentive, especially a staff member named Ms. Noy, who pays attention to detail and provides impressive service. Thank you for the beautiful and delicious birthday cake. Thank you to the kitchen staff as well.

name: The Landmark Bangkok
detail: This was a last-minute booking due to a flight delay, but it turned out to be the kindest and most comfortable place among the three accommodations I stayed at during this trip. Although it's an older establishment and not a trendy new hotel or an Instagram-worthy spot, the details of older Bangkok hotels that can’t be seen in newer ones are great, and the service from the staff is very comforting. In fact, it’s not uncommon to encounter expensive places where faucets splash a lot, toilets are too high, or amenities that feel overpriced and barely useful. However, here everything felt just right, not too little and not too much, tailored perfectly for guests. They allowed early check-in two hours before our scheduled time and offered late check-out at 4 PM. Additionally, you can enjoy cocktails and a variety of finger foods for free while watching the night view from the 31st-floor lounge. The swimming pool is 2.6 meters deep... Later, I borrowed some tape for my luggage, and they were more than happy to lend it. Thanks to Clovis at the reception, I was well-fed with a really delicious latte, complete with rich milk foam, and I arrived at the airport with ample time to spare. It's located right in front of Nana Station, making it easy to go anywhere, and I was truly disappointed to have only spent one night there. The breakfast might not have a wide variety, but it is prepared with care rather than just relying on seasonings, and the coffee is absolutely the best. Sipping coffee while gazing at the skyscrapers in the morning made me not want to go home. I recommend this place to those who miss classic hotel service. The lounge view of the city is stunning, so skip the rooftop bar and come here instead!

name: Elite Hotel Asok Sukhumvit 20
detail: If u looking for staycation elite is one of the best locations Ive been. Close to all malls n. Night market

name: Ramada Graand Swiss Sukhumvit 11
detail: It is about a 3-minute walk from BTS Nana. The surrounding area has many restaurants, massage shops, and convenience stores, making it very convenient. I could hear music from the shop downstairs, but it became quiet around 11 o'clock. The room was small but clean, and since I was alone, it wasn't particularly an issue. Breakfast is 375 baht payable on the day (which is 1.36 times more expensive compared to last year), but I felt that the content and price did not match well.

name: The Bless Hotel & Residence
detail: This hotel is conveniently located near Phrom Phong Station. It is just a few minutes' walk to large commercial facilities like EmSphere and Emporium, making it very convenient for shopping. There are many massage shops, restaurants, and places to enjoy at night in the surrounding area, and since it is a place with many Japanese residents, it's reassuring that Japanese can be understood at some places. With BTS Phrom Phong Station nearby, accessing various areas of Bangkok is easy, making it a convenient location for both sightseeing and shopping. Although the building itself shows some age, it is well-maintained. The guest rooms are quite spacious and stylishly decorated. There was also a sofa, which allowed me to relax after returning to the hotel. The bathroom has separate shower and bathtub facilities, and the toilet is equipped with a washlet. The amenities made it comfortable for Japanese guests, as NHK is also available on the television. Considering the current hotel prices in central Bangkok, I think there are not many hotels in this price range that offer this location and room size. I felt that the balance of location, size, and price is very good. The only disappointment was that there was no hot water from the shower during my stay. The cold water shower was very chilly, so I would appreciate it if this could be improved. Besides that, I was very satisfied and can recommend this hotel to those who want a reasonably priced spacious room around Phrom Phong.
